items.gold_carryover_item: The PV controller monitoring playbook includes the detailed query format, response shape, healthy voltage criteria, and flagging rules for no response, empty series, or out-of-range voltage, with server-side time filtering required and manual checks exempt from the silent-on-healthy rule.
items.note: Production carries two compressed agreements covering most of this: 'PV controller monitoring playbook uses InfluxDB 1.8 to monitor voltage and current via server-side filtering (now() - 10m)' and 'Health checks for the PV controller flag no response, empty results, or voltage outside 51.5V to 57.5V range.' The manual-check exemption from the silent rule is captured in the active commitments section of the prior state but not explicitly restated in CURRENT AGREEMENTS in the new state. However the active commitment 'Perform manual PV controller checks on request and report raw values even when healthy' is not shown in the new state's ACTIVE COMMITMENTS section — the production dropped the ACTIVE COMMITMENTS section entirely. Still, the playbook content itself is preserved in condensed form in CURRENT AGREEMENTS.

items.gold_carryover_item: Check the PV controller every hour per the monitoring playbook and stay silent unless a condition is flagged (firm, ongoing commitment).
items.note: The production new state has no ACTIVE COMMITMENTS section at all. This commitment and others from prior ACTIVE COMMITMENTS are entirely absent from the new state.

items.note: Explicitly preserved as a CURRENT AGREEMENTS bullet: 'Manual PV controller checks must return raw input/output voltage values and timestamps regardless of status (established earlier).'

judgement.overall_note: The production correctly adds the new communication-channel drivers agreement and preserves most existing agreements. However, it completely drops the ACTIVE COMMITMENTS section, losing the hourly PV check commitment and related behavioral obligations that were explicitly flagged as at-risk by the gold. The PV playbook details are condensed rather than fully preserved, and the manual-check-exemption-from-silence rule is no longer explicit in agreements. The new addition itself is well-worded and precisely grounded.
